chunks: A man came to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) and said: 'O Messenger of God, what is knowledge?' He said: 'Silence.' He said: 'Then what?' He said: 'Intent listening.' He said: 'Then what?' He said: 'Memorisation.' He said: 'Then what?' He said: 'Acting upon it.' He said: 'Then what, O Messenger of God?' He said: 'Propagating it.'

key_terms.الإنصات: Insat — attentive, reverential silence before a teacher; the first stage of acquiring knowledge
key_terms.الاستماع: Istima' — active, intent listening; deeper engagement than mere hearing
key_terms.الحفظ: Hifz — memorisation; preservation of knowledge in the heart
key_terms.العمل به: Al-'amal bihi — acting upon knowledge; translating it into practice
key_terms.نشره: Nashruhu — spreading/propagating it; disseminating knowledge to others

ai.seo_question: What are the five stages of knowledge according to the Prophet Muhammad in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This prophetic tradition, transmitted through Imam al-Sadiq (AS) from his forefathers, presents a dialogue between a man and the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) in which knowledge is defined through five sequential stages: attentive silence, intent listening, memorisation, acting upon it, and propagating it to others. This pedagogical framework — likely delivered in the early Medinan period when the Prophet was actively teaching the fledgling Muslim community — reflects the classical Islamic understanding that knowledge is not merely intellectual acquisition but a complete cycle culminating in its dissemination. The original audience would have understood 'knowledge' (al-'ilm) primarily as religious and ethical knowledge obligatory for every Muslim, and 'propagating it' (nashruhu) as fulfilling the duty of teaching others, echoing the Quranic injunction to convey the message.
